patch.value: An annotation edit accepts text copied from a strings_compacted read, so a read-modify-write round trip silently truncates the stored entry

Found 2026-11-11 on PR 1708 (a Greptile finding). To correct one timestamp, I read the newest pm-7zs0 comment with 'pm comments pm-7zs0 --json', replaced one word and wrote it back with 'pm comments pm-7zs0 --edit 270 --file <text>'. The default 3,000-token output budget had compacted that 900-character comment to a prefix ending in '…'. read_output reported strings_compacted: true and the page said truncated: true, but nothing stopped the edit, so the stored comment lost its second half. The same round trip is natural for notes and learnings, and for any agent that fixes a word in place. Duplicate check: searched output budget, compaction, truncation and annotation edit; pm-8eclqf, pm-gh1552 and pm-gh1478 (closed) bound and preserve reads, but none guards the write side of a compacted read.

An annotation --edit whose replacement text equals a compacted projection of the stored entry (a prefix ending in the compaction marker) is refused with a typed code naming the --output-budget unbounded or --limit read that returns the full text; Compacted strings in budgeted reads carry a marker the write path can recognise; Edits of genuinely new text ending in an ellipsis still succeed
A read-modify-write edit of an annotation never stores a budget-compacted prefix
pm comments --edit stored the compacted prefix of a 900-character comment without warning
